value: Alcoholic participants had significantly smaller total cerebellar white matter volume than nonalcoholic controls, with a 6.1% reduction overall; alcoholic women had 7.7% larger total cerebellar volumes than alcoholic men.
These findings support prior reports that cerebellar white matter volume is smaller in individuals with chronic alcoholism histories relative to individuals with no such histories.
